bank_name: South Bangla Agriculture & Commerce Bank PLC
period_note: SBAC BANK LIMITED (pre-2023 name). HALF-YEARLY unaudited financial statement -- balance sheet is the 30-June-2016 period-end snapshot (reported), compared against the prior 31-December-2015 audited year-end. Income-statement items are CUMULATIVE from 1 January 2016 (the statement's own 'From 01 January 2016 to 30 June 2016' column; this is the bank's only Q2 presentation -- there is no separate discrete-quarter column in this filing), placed in the _Q2 slot per this dataset's Half-Yearly-as-Q2 convention. No subsidiary existed yet in 2016 (SBAC Bank Investment Limited was not incorporated until 2021 per this bank's sources.json), so this is unambiguously Solo/Standalone -- there is no Consolidated-vs-Solo distinction to make for this period. Equity is presented across SIX components in this year's format (paid-up capital, statutory reserve, general reserve [nil], other/revaluation reserve, 'Current year's profit', and retained earnings brought forward) rather than the four-component layout seen in this bank's FY2025 quarterly filings -- 'Current year's profit' here is the same figure as net profit after taxation for the period, not a separate balance; the five non-zero components sum exactly to total_equity. No classified-loans/NPL disclosure is present in this simple 4-page filing (no notes section) -- recorded as a gap, consistent with the FY2014/FY2015 classified-loan gaps already documented in this bank's sources.json. No capital adequacy (CRAR/RWA) disclosure either -- Basel III Pillar III disclosures are annual-report-only throughout this dataset's SBACBANK coverage. This filing (unlike the FY2025 vintage) extracted natively via pdftotext -layout, but the two-column layout came out interleaved/misaligned (labels separated from values, e.g. the TOTAL ASSETS row itself failed to extract as a number); all figures below were instead read directly off 200dpi page images for accuracy, with the native pdftotext extraction kept in the archived .txt only as a secondary reference.
